title: Team
text:
The EDM Program is an executive-supported team with a deep knowledgebase of data governance and data management. The team excels at working on multiple efforts at once, dedicated to improving data stewardship, data management, and ultimately science for NOAA Fisheries. Furthermore, the EDM Program’s well-established, collaborative relationship across the FMCs, NOAA writ large, FIS, external partners like the FINs (Fishery Information Network), and OCIO uniquely positions the program to drive enterprise-wide data management strategies.
Want to collaborate or contribute? Get in touch

title: Data Policies & Guidance
text: Federal data policies and practical guidance to help NOAA staff understand their obligations and how to meet them.

title: Data Policies & Guidance
text:
Federal Data Policies
These laws and directives establish the legal framework for how federal agencies must collect, manage, share, and preserve data.

Evidence Act (2018)
Foundations for Evidence-Based Policymaking Act — requires agencies to designate Chief Data Officers, develop learning agendas, and make data available for evidence-building.
What it means for you: Data collected with federal resources must be managed well enough to be reused for future policy and research.
View Policy →


Information Quality Act (IQA)
Requires federal agencies to ensure the quality, objectivity, utility, and integrity of information they disseminate.
What it means for you: Data products must meet documented quality standards before public release.
View Policy →


OPEN Government Data Act
Part of the Evidence Act — requires federal data to be published as machine-readable, open data by default.
What it means for you: FAIR data principles are a legal requirement, not just a best practice.
View Policy →


OSTP Open Science Memo (2022)
“Ensuring Free, Immediate, and Equitable Access to Federally Funded Research” — requires data underlying publications to be publicly accessible at time of publication.
What it means for you: Plan for open data sharing from the start of every project.
View Policy →


OMB M-19-15
Updated guidance on IQA implementation, including peer review requirements for influential scientific information.
What it means for you: Peer review and quality documentation are required for disseminated scientific products.
View Policy →


NAO 212-15B
NOAA Administrative Order establishing requirements for full data lifecycle management across all NOAA data domains.
What it means for you: The primary NOAA policy document your data management practices must comply with.
View Policy →

title: Data Policies & Guidance
text:
Data Guidance
Practical guidance documents to help NOAA scientists and data managers implement good data practices. Links will be added as guidance is finalized.

NOAA Fisheries Data Preservation Guidance
Internal - Published 2025 All NOAA Fisheries Data Stewards?
NOAA Fisheries FMCs must quickly assess which data may be at a level of risk. NOAA Fisheries program/laboratory/data leaders must work with their appropriate Assistant Chief Data Officers (ACDOs) to identify these data, ensure that a minimum level of information for these data is recorded, and secure these data in appropriate storage.
Read Guidance →


Guidance for Adding New Metadata Records to InPort
Internal - Published 2026 All NOAA Fisheries Data Users
Step-by-step guidance for writing Data Management Plans (DMPs) that satisfy NSF, NIH, and NOAA requirements.
Read Guidance →


Metadata Completeness and Quality Checks
Internal - Published 2024 NOAA Fisheries Data Stewards
The NOAA Metadata Rubric evaluates the presence or absence of content in a standard NOAA compliant metadata record.
Read Guidance →

title: Data Lifecycle
text: Understanding the data lifecycle is foundational to good science. Every stage — from planning through reuse — has implications for the quality, reproducibility, and long-term value of your data.

title: Data Lifecycle
text:
Why Data Management Matters
Good data management is not just a compliance requirement — it is what makes science trustworthy, reproducible, and useful beyond a single project.








Framework
What it requires
Why it matters to you




FAIR Data Principles
Data must be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable
Extends the scientific value of your work; enables others to build on it


OSTP Open Science Memo (2022)
Federally funded research data must be publicly accessible by default
NOAA data is a public asset — it must be managed well enough to share


Evidence Act (2018)
Federal data must be available for future evidence-building and policy
Data collected with federal resources must be reusable, not just stored


Information Quality Act (IQA)
Disseminated data must meet documented quality and objectivity standards
Lifecycle practices — versioning, QC, documentation — are how you comply


Gold Standard Science
Results must be peer-reviewed, reproducible, and transparently documented
Data lifecycle management is how you operationalize this commitment

title: Data Lifecycle
text:
The Data Lifecycle
The NOAA Data Life Cycle model (Figure 1, NAO 212-15B Data Management Handbook) provides the official framework for managing NOAA data as a strategic asset. It consists of six primary components and four cross-cutting components that apply throughout.
